newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil requires 11.1 mln new B Band cellular lines.
newsitem.headline: Brazil requires 11.1 mln new B Band cellular lines.

text.p: Brazil's private B Band cellular telephone operators must install at least 11.1 million new lines nationwide and may hold contracts on no more than two concession areas, one large and one small, the government said.

Tender documents released by the Communications Ministry also said firms formed to operate on the B Band frequency must be 51 percent Brazilian-owned and have a net worth equal to 10 percent of the concession base price.
The government plans to take bids on the 10 B Band concessions on March 31 with contract signings tentatively scheduled for May or June.
The bid documents, made available Monday, also laid out some 3.7 billion reais in base price contracts to operate the concessions.
Winners will be picked according to which has the lowest rate and the highest concession prices, weightings of 60 percent and 40 percent respectively, the bid specifications said.

They said a winning consortium may hold no more than two contracts: one among the six concessions covering densely populated areas and one among four serving Brazil's large, sparsely populated north and northeast regions.
The groups that win bidding on the 15-year concessions will see no competition until at least December 31, 1999 from companies "using the public telecommunications network."
In the coming years, the government plans to privatize the cellular services now operated by the federal Telebras system.
The bid documents said B Band operators also must present a basic service plan and maximum rate, which may not be adjusted for at least 12 months.
The firms may, however, offer differentiated rates, including discounts, promotional rates, seasonal rates and special low rates for low-demand periods, they added.

According to the tender documents, groups operating the concessions covering metropolitan Sao Paulo and greater Sao Paulo state each must install 1.8 million new terminals and have a net worth of 60 million reais, or 10 percent of the base prices.
In the states of Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo, the consortium must have a net worth of 50 million reais and the operator must install 1.5 million new terminals, it said.
For the remaining seven concession areas, it stipulated the following number of new terminals and minimum net worth:
Minas Gerais state: 1.2 million terminals and 40 million reais.
Parana and Santa Catarina states: a million lines; 33 million reais.
Rio Grande do Sul state: a million lines; 33 million reais.
Goais, Tocantins, Mato Grosso, Rondonia and Acre states and the federal district: 800,000 lines; 27 million reais.
Amazonas, Roraima, Amapa, Para and Maranhao states: 600,000 lines; 20 million reais.
Bahia and Sergipe states: 700,000 lines; 23 million reais.
Piaui, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco and Alagoas states: 700,000 lines; 23 million reais.
It did not say how long the concession holders would have to meet the goals for installing new terminals.
The tender rules -- four phone book-sized catalogues -- are available at the ministry for 200 reais or on the Internet at http:/w.w.w.mc.gov.br, according to officials.
((--Michael Christie, Brasilia newsroom 5561 223 0358))
